nodes.body: The new contract location conflicts with this skill's response-pricing definition at lines 495–510 and PDR-140 clause 3, both of which still make opening working notes the firing gate. Because this paragraph now says a working-notes declaration only bounds the seat, shepherds have two incompatible instructions for activating the state machine. Out-of-scope observation: the authoritative location or an explicit copy relationship needs to be reconciled with PDR-140.

**In scope, over-bar** (prong two: two incompatible instructions for activating the state machine). Cured in `SHA:39c627107`: the single definition — the state machine's §Response pricing block — now names the description's §Scope as the intake's home, "the shepherd's opening working notes in PDR-140 clause 3's sense, and the one surface every reviewer reads"; Phase 2 cites that block instead of restating it. PDR-140 itself is unchanged and out of this pull request's scope: the body is the opening working notes the clause names, so the relationship is a reading, not a conflict. Noted with thanks that this finding arrived labelled as an out-of-scope observation — the instruction under test is being read. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

The review focus says this ordering is stated once in Phase 4 and merely cited here, but these lines restate both the ordering and the remedy rule. That creates a second normative copy which can drift; it already switches between testing the observation and deciding scope from the remedy. Keep this rule as a direct pointer to the canonical Phase 4 instruction.

**In scope, over-bar** (a second normative copy that can drift — §Documentation Is Infrastructure names DRY in doctrine as a real defect, and the review focus invited exactly this check). Cured in `SHA:39c627107`: the rule's preamble is now a pointer to `pr-lifecycle` §Phase 4's scope-first test, carrying no ordering or remedy rule of its own. Evidence class READ.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify observations before routing them**

For an out-of-scope remedy attached to a false or mischaracterised observation, these lines now route the finding to a durable named home without verification. This contradicts both step 1 immediately below and PDR-140 clause 1 (`.agent/practice-core/decision-records/PDR-140-review-response-pricing.md:94-104`), which requires every finding to receive first-hand verification before routing or rejection. Scope can determine where a verified issue is handled, but skipping verification can preserve false findings in tickets or registers.

That block explicitly says amendments belong there rather than in phase-local restatements, so the two instructions can still produce the unbounded review loop this change is intended to prevent; update the authoritative block to name `§Scope`.

That rule explicitly permits genuine shared state including doctrine (`coordination-branch-24h-lifetime.md:50-56`) and excludes source lanes and plans under active edit, so treating every doctrine change as a work product makes the ceremony contradict its source of truth and unnecessarily splits valid shared-state work.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Test remedies against declared scope, not artefact growth**

When the declared `## Scope` expressly includes work that adds content—for example, edge-case coverage for the parser being changed—these lines nevertheless classify adding coverage as a scope finding and require no cure here. That can route a real, in-scope defect merely because its cure enlarges the artefact; the deciding test must remain whether the remedy exceeds the declared scope, not whether it adds coverage or other material.

These lines instead route the observation without a cure whenever the reviewer's proposed remedy exceeds `§Scope`, allowing misleading changed doctrine to merge; discard that proposed remedy, but still derive an in-scope correction or removal for every finding that clears the declared bar.

**Out of scope, below-bar.** Rejected, no write. The observation is true as a reading of the layers: the three-way enumeration at these lines is the owner's ratified 2026-07-25 disposition ruling, quoted verbatim, and its "anything else → ticket" default predates PDR-140 clause 1, which made reject-with-rationale-or-route the default and which the state machine's §Response pricing block names as the owner of the clauses. Phase 4's new sentences follow PDR-140; the enumeration is the older layer beneath it, and a shepherd reads both with the block's "PDR-140 owns the clauses" in force. The remedy — rewriting the owner's ruling text — exceeds this pull request's declared scope ("the minimum that makes the existing doctrine fire"), and no reader acts wrongly before the next verification point because the pricing block already governs. Reconciling the enumeration's wording with PDR-140 is a PDR-140 follow-up, noted in this seat's napkin on the coordination branch, not a cure here. Evidence class READ.
